blocks.title: Toxicity
blocks.text: Toxicity is the extent to which a substance can harm an organism or the environment.
A material may be toxic during its production, its use and its final disposal. Toxicity is measured by the extent and type of hazard that a material may cause, and there are several types of hazard.

items: Health hazards: a substance damages health on exposure. Chromium compounds, for example, are carcinogens (cause cancer) and mutagens (change DNA and genes) and cause respiratory problems; some additives in plastics can cause hormonal problems.

Physical hazards: harm due to physical or chemical properties, to buildings, humans, ecosystems and the environment; for example a flammable or explosive material can harm people and forests or damage a building.

Environmental hazards: long-term harm to aquatic life or the environment. Heavy metals such as lead, mercury and cadmium can leach into soil and groundwater and are dangerous to plants, land animals, fish and other aquatic organisms.
